US Navy raises Gecko contract ceiling to $300 million for ship inspection

Komodo measures steel beneath deck coatings without stripping them, supporting maintenance planning before dry-dock work.

The Robot Report ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

An increase to the existing ceiling

The US Navy and General Services Administration raised Gecko Robotics’ five-year IDIQ ceiling from $71 million to $300 million, according to details DefenseScoop verified with the company. The original scope covered 18 Pacific Fleet ships; expansion will support the Atlantic Surface Fleet. A ceiling is not guaranteed orders or revenue.

Measuring steel beneath coatings

Komodo travels over decks and uses electromagnetic acoustic transducer technology to measure steel thickness beneath non-skid coatings without stripping them first. It helps identify corrosion or structural degradation and can gather evidence while a ship remains afloat, before its maintenance period begins.

Inspection evidence shapes repair plans

Gecko combines measurements from robots, drones and sensors with analysis software to help engineers prioritize repairs and avoid unnecessary replacement. Time and cost benefits depend on the vessel and actual work. The higher ceiling expands potential use rather than proving identical savings on every ship.
